title: The objection: the Psalm's words are the Savior's, not the Holy Spirit's
english: It was necessary for Scripture to be fulfilled, which the Holy Spirit foretold through the mouth of David about Judas (Acts 1:16). In that psalm the things about Judas are written. Someone might say that the Holy Spirit is not speaking, for clearly the words belong to the Savior when he says: “O God, do not pass over my praise in silence, for the mouth of the sinner and the mouth of the deceitful have opened against me” (Psalm 108:2 LXX / Psalm 109:2 Hebrew), and so on until: “And let another take his office” (Psalm 108:8 LXX / Psalm 109:8 Hebrew).

orientation: Origen has just cited Acts 1:16, where Peter says the Scripture about Judas had to be fulfilled, and now he raises an objection about who is speaking in the Psalm.
